hook: Follow a lively radio debate and keep track of who wants what, who objects, and where the two sides finally meet.
intro: A radio debate on a car-free city centre — a moderator, a campaigner (Frau Keller) and a retail spokesman (Herr Brandt) — heard once, about four minutes long. Following a debate like this — on the radio, at a council meeting, round a dinner table — means tracking who argues what, where each side moves, and where they end up agreeing. Frau Keller opens with a demand (dass der Bereich innerhalb des Rings gesperrt wird) and evidence from other cities; Herr Brandt objects with the customers who come from the countryside; she answers with a survey (nur ein Viertel der Kunden kommt mit dem Auto); he insists on the order of steps (zuerst den öffentlichen Verkehr ausbauen); she proposes a compromise (mit einzelnen Straßen zu beginnen). Note each side by its name, fix one keyword per move, and listen for the moderator’s summary at the end — the „einig / uneinig“ sentence is always a question.
tips[0].title: Befürworter / Gegner / Moderator — three voices, three keywords
tips[0].text: Frau Keller: pro (Luft, Sicherheit, Zahlen aus Gent). Herr Brandt: contra (Kunden vom Land, Einkaufszentrum am Stadtrand). Moderatorin: the summary (einig, dass … / uneinig darüber, wann …). Note them as you hear them, with the speaker’s name.
tips[0].check.why: Cleaner air and safer streets are arguments for the car-free plan, so this is the supporter's keyword set.
tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Moderator
tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Befürworter (for)
tips[0].visual.moves[2].label: Gegner (against)
tips[0].visual.moves[3].label: Kompromiss
tips[1].title: Reported speech signals
tips[1].text: fordern, dass …; widersprechen; das Argument höre ich oft, aber …; ich sage nicht, dass …; wir schlagen vor, … zu …; damit könnte ich leben — the verbs tell you whose move it is, and whether it is a demand, an objection, a concession or a proposal.
tips[1].check.why: Ich sage nicht, dass … grants a point; aber … then brings the objection.
tips[2].title: Eröffnung / Einwand / Kompromiss / Bilanz
tips[2].text: The debate’s structure: what is demanded first (Eröffnung), what the other side objects (Einwand), what is offered (Kompromiss), what the moderator records as agreed and not agreed (Bilanz). Map the questions to these four.
tips[2].check.why: Recording what both sides agree and disagree on is the moderator's closing summary, the Bilanz.
remember[0]: Label each voice by name; one keyword per move.
remember[1]: The moderator’s „einig / uneinig“ summary at the end is always asked.
exam: Radio discussions with several speakers are a standard listening text in the B2 exam — and on any evening of German talk radio.
tips[0].check.q: In a debate on a car-free centre, a speaker says: „Ohne Autos wird die Luft besser und die Straßen werden sicherer.“ Which voice is this?
tips[1].check.q: „Ich sage nicht, dass der Plan schlecht ist, aber er kommt zu früh.“ What kind of move is this?
tips[1].check.options[0]: a concession followed by an objection
tips[1].check.answer: a concession followed by an objection
